blocks.text: Yes — Airbnb and other short-term rental accommodation (STRA) is legal in Bondi and right across New South Wales, but it comes with real rules, and the one that catches most people out is a 180-day cap. Bondi sits inside the Waverley local government area, which is part of Greater Sydney, so the state's tighter Greater Sydney limits apply here. I get asked about this constantly by would-be hosts and by guests wondering why a listing suddenly went dark for the season, so here's how it actually works.
Hosted vs non-hosted — the distinction that decides everything

NSW splits STRA into two categories, and which one you fall into changes the rules dramatically. "Hosted" means the host lives on the premises while guests stay — think renting out a spare room while you're home. "Non-hosted" means the host isn't there — the classic "whole place" Airbnb where you hand over the keys and disappear.

Hosted STRA in Bondi has no annual day limit — you can host as many nights as you like, provided you meet the other requirements. Non-hosted STRA is where the cap bites: in Greater Sydney (which includes Waverley and therefore Bondi), a whole-property listing is limited to a maximum of 180 days per year when the host isn't present.

blocks.title: How the 180 days are counted
blocks.text: The count runs over a 12-month registration period, not the calendar year. And here's the part hosts often miss: any single booking of 21 or more consecutive days to the same guest is excluded from the 180-day tally. Long-stay guests — someone between homes, a visiting academic — don't eat into your cap.
You must register before you list

This is the step people skip and later regret. Before you advertise or take a single booking, the property has to be registered on the NSW STRA Register via the NSW Planning Portal. You're issued a property ID that must appear on the online listing — platforms like Airbnb and Stayz expect to see it. Registration also requires you to confirm the dwelling meets fire-safety standards and to agree to the mandatory Code of Conduct.

items: Register the property on the NSW STRA Register before advertising.
Display your STRA property ID on every listing.
Meet the fire-safety requirements for the dwelling.
Comply with the mandatory Code of Conduct (in force since December 2020).
Renew your registration annually to stay active.

blocks.text: There are registration and annual renewal fees. Because government fees can change, I won't quote a figure that might be stale by the time you read this — check the current amounts on the Service NSW or NSW Planning Portal pages linked below before you pay.
The Code of Conduct and the two-strikes rule

The Code of Conduct sets minimum standards of behaviour for everyone in the market — hosts, guests, platforms and letting agents — and it has teeth. It covers noise, disruptive behaviour and neighbour complaints. Serious or repeated breaches can land a host or guest on an exclusion register, and a "two strikes" principle means two serious breaches within two years can trigger a five-year ban from the STRA market. It's not just paperwork; it's genuinely enforced.

If your Bondi apartment is in a strata building, check the by-laws before you count on Airbnb income. An owners corporation can pass a by-law prohibiting short-term letting in lots that are NOT the host's principal place of residence. Plenty of beachside blocks here have done exactly that — a valid state registration won't override a lawful strata ban.

items.a: Yes. Short-term rental accommodation is legal across NSW, including Bondi, provided the property is registered on the NSW STRA Register, meets fire-safety requirements, and the host follows the Code of Conduct. Bondi is in the Waverley LGA within Greater Sydney, so the Greater Sydney rules — including the 180-day non-hosted cap — apply.

items.q: What is the 180-day limit and does it apply to Bondi?
items.a: In Greater Sydney, non-hosted (whole-property, host-not-present) STRA is capped at 180 days over a 12-month registration period. Bondi falls inside Greater Sydney, so yes, it applies. Hosted stays, where you live on-site, have no day cap. Bookings of 21+ consecutive days to the same guest don't count toward the 180.

items.q: Do I need to register my Bondi property?
items.a: Yes — registration on the NSW STRA Register via the NSW Planning Portal is mandatory before you advertise or take bookings. You'll receive a property ID that must be displayed on your listing, and registration must be renewed annually.

items.q: Can my strata building ban short-term rentals?
items.a: It can. An owners corporation may adopt a by-law prohibiting short-term letting in lots that are not the host's principal place of residence. If your apartment isn't your main home, a strata ban can lawfully stop you letting it short-term even if you're otherwise registered.

items.q: What happens if a host breaks the rules?
items.a: Breaches of the Code of Conduct can lead to penalties and listing on an exclusion register. Under the two-strikes principle, two serious breaches within two years can result in a five-year ban from participating in the STRA market.

blocks.text: The short version: renting your Bondi place on Airbnb is legal, but treat registration, the 180-day non-hosted cap and your strata by-laws as non-negotiable homework. For the current official detail — fees, the register and any policy updates — go to the NSW Planning Portal and Service NSW rather than a host forum.
